low_power_modes_summary.HS_active: HS payload streaming on Data Lanes + DDR Clock Lane; highest current; used for pixel-stream and large command bursts.
low_power_modes_summary.LP_active: Low-Power signaling (≤ 10 Mbps); used for forward escape (LPDT, Trigger, Reset) on Data Lane 0 and all reverse-direction Acknowledge / Error Report / Read Response / TE.
low_power_modes_summary.Stop_state_LP11: Both Dp and Dn driven HIGH (1.2 V CMOS); near-static; minimal current; baseline idle state between bursts.
low_power_modes_summary.ULPS: Ultra-Low Power State; lane held LP-00 indefinitely; receiver in deep sleep; entered via LP Escape command; lowest current state.
low_power_modes_summary.Non_Continuous_Clock_Mode: Clock Lane returns to LP-11 between bursts to save clock-tree power; optional support — host explicitly chooses this mode.
low_power_modes_summary.Continuous_Clock_Mode: Clock Lane stays in HS forever; lower latency at the cost of higher power.
low_power_modes_summary.Video_Mode_BLLP_LP_substitution: In Video Mode, if sufficient time exists during HBP / HFP / blanking, the bus may transition to LP instead of sending Blanking Packets — substantial power saving.

ulps_specification_inherited_from_d_phy.exit_signaling: Source drives LP-10 (Mark-One) for ≥ T-WAKEUP (≈ 1 ms minimum); both ends return to LP-11.
ulps_specification_inherited_from_d_phy.minimum_duration: Unbounded — peripheral may stay in ULPS indefinitely for deep sleep.

shutdown_and_turn_on_commands.shutdown_peripheral_DT: 0x22 — Short Packet command; turns off display in Video Mode display module for power saving. The interface SHALL remain powered in order to receive the turn-on / wake-up command.
shutdown_and_turn_on_commands.turn_on_peripheral_DT: 0x32 — Short Packet command; turns on display in Video Mode display module for normal display operation.

color_mode_commands.color_mode_off_DT: 0x02 — Short Packet command; returns a Video Mode display module from low-color mode to normal display operation.
color_mode_commands.color_mode_on_DT: 0x12 — Short Packet command; switches a Video Mode display module to a low-color mode for power saving.

fields.command_mode_low_power_substitute: A Video Mode display module may include a simplified form of Command Mode operation with a reduced-size or partial frame buffer, so the display module can shut down the streaming video interface and continue to refresh the screen from a small local frame buffer at reduced resolution and pixel depth. The local frame buffer SHALL be loaded prior to interface shutdown.
power_classes_of_implementations: Mobile-phone Command Mode display — aggressive Non-Continuous Clock + ULPS + Color Mode On for battery life.
Mobile-phone Video Mode display — Continuous Clock (or Non-Continuous with BLLP-to-LP substitution) for low latency.
Tablet / handheld with on-panel frame buffer — Command Mode with periodic refresh writes; ULPS between writes.
fields.notes: DSI v1.01.00 inherits all PHY-level power modes (HS, LP, Stop, ULPS, Non-Continuous Clock) from D-PHY. DSI adds protocol-level power-control commands — Shutdown Peripheral (0x22), Turn On Peripheral (0x32), Color Mode Off / On (0x02 / 0x12) — and the Video Mode BLLP-to-LP substitution mechanism that allows the bus to enter LP during horizontal blanking intervals when timing permits. Power management for the panel itself is exposed via DCS commands carried inside DSI 0x05 / 0x15 / 0x39 packets.
